summary: Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. Supplied English is project machine translation, retained verbatim where quoted; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.

Kməḥṭarminalle is a finite Infectum form with k-, 1pl subject and a plural object suffix -lle. The left-dislocated aš šexawiye is resumed on the verb; there is no independent l-marked object NP in this sentence.

Provisionally retain I for this four-consonant loan, following the glossary convention illustrated by trǧm I mtarǧamle/mtarǧəm. This is an entry classification, not a claim that ḥṭrm has the inherited triliteral I paradigm. No unobserved Preterit, Detransitive, Imperativ or Infinitiv is supplied.

Probable contact lexeme corresponding to Arabic iḥtaram “respect”, with the inserted consonant retained in the Turoyo root representation. The written token has ṭ; related məḥtarmo under ʔṯy has t. Preserve the source spelling, and leave the lemma normalization and etymology for confirmation.

Read-only lookup found no ḥṭrm or ḥtrm root entry. The ḥrm 1/2 entries concern deprivation/prohibition and excommunication, not honour, so this token is not assigned to them. Related məḥtarmo in an ʔṯy example supports prior adjectival use but does not provide another finite attestation or an independently quotable Jan example.

This is an ordinary lexical verb with an animate patient, not a light verb plus noun collocation. The passage concerns honour shown by Syriacs to sheikhs; one token does not establish a special religious sense or a register restriction.
